headline_marked: [[US websites]] serve 3x more trackers than EU sites, study finds
headline: US websites serve 3x more trackers than EU sites, study finds
summary: A new test reveals US visitors face significantly more high-risk tracking requests and third-party cookies compared to EU visitors, with some sites showing cookie banners only to Europeans.
details: A recent study comparing website behavior from Virginia, US, and Frankfurt, Germany, found that US visitors encountered approximately three times more high-risk tracking requests and four times more third-party cookies before any consent was given.

The test, conducted on October 14, 2026, involved loading the same 200 websites from both locations. It also revealed that 21 sites displayed cookie banners exclusively to visitors in Frankfurt, while those in Virginia never saw them.

This disparity highlights how many websites alter their privacy practices based on a visitor's perceived location, often determined by IP address. This can lead to inconsistent privacy experiences and potential issues with compliance, especially concerning signals like California's Global Privacy Control.

For website owners, this means that testing from a single location can mask significant privacy problems. To ensure comprehensive compliance and a consistent user experience, sites should be tested from each major visitor region, both before and after consent is given.

headline_marked: Firefox Smart Window [[adds AI form filling]] and website monitoring
headline: Firefox Smart Window adds AI form filling and website monitoring
summary: Mozilla's opt-in AI browsing tool now helps users fill out forms and keep tabs on webpage changes, enhancing productivity.
details: Mozilla has rolled out two new features for Firefox's opt-in AI-powered Smart Window experience. These updates aim to streamline browsing by automating tasks and providing proactive information.

The first new capability is AI-powered form autofill. Smart Window can now intelligently fill in personal details on web forms, drawing information from sources like LinkedIn profiles to save users time and effort when signing up for services or applying for jobs.

The second feature introduces website monitoring. Smart Window can track changes on specific webpages, alerting users when content is updated. This is particularly useful for monitoring job postings, price changes, or news articles.

These enhancements are part of Mozilla's ongoing effort to integrate AI into Firefox in a user-friendly and privacy-conscious manner. The Smart Window features are opt-in, giving users control over their data and browsing experience.
